blocks.text: B2-10 · Argumentative texts
Lesson overview

The articles of opinion ( ⁧مَقَالُ رَأْيٍ⁩ ), editorials ( ⁧اِفْتِتَاحِيَّة⁩ ) and headings ( ⁧عَمُود⁩ ) are the part of the newspaper in which it is discussed: the author supports a thesis, brings arguments, responds to objections and draws a conclusion. For an analyst they are valuable, because they show how to think in a country about a topic; But they must be read knowing how to distinguish the thesis from the arguments, the solid arguments from the weak ones, the apparent concession from the true. In this unit you learn the structure of an argumentative text , the correlations of the cause , consequence , addition and concession ( ⁧فَضْلًا عَنْ⁩ , ⁧وَمِنْ ثَمَّ⁩ , ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ … ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ …, ⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ⁩ … ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ ...), the most frequent types of argument and fallacies, and start writing your own argumentative text. Four weeks, in parallel with EGY-15.

rows: B2 · Module B2.2 Attribution and certainty
20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 193–196), plus the EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)69), voice synthesis scripts, tutor sessions
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. identify in an article of opinion thesis, arguments, examples, objections, rebuttals and conclusion;
2. use and recognize the argumentative connections of fuṣḥā, including concessionary constructions ( ⁧صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ⁩ …
3. classify the arguments (data, e.g. authorities, consequences, comparison) and assess their soundness;
4. recognizing the most common fallacies (generalization, false dilemma, attack on the person);
5. write an argumentative text of 250 words with a clear structure.
Four-week plan.

⁧وَإِذَا كَانَ⁩ … ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ ... is one of the most typical structures of Arabic argumentative prose and one of the most difficult to translate: it is not a hypothetical period (s... then... ....) but a concessionary comparison: if it is true that..., it is also true that... . , , while..., ... ... .... You recognize it because the first part is true.
5. Dialogue 2 · The center without car
Yāsmīn and Luca discuss, for exercise, whether to close the center of Milan to cars. Everyone must use at least one concession.

rows: ⁧يَاسْمِين: أَنَا أُؤَيِّدُ إِغْلَاقَ وَسَطِ المَدِينَةِ أَمَامَ السَّيَّارَاتِ. أَوَّلًا لِأَنَّ الهَوَاءَ سَيُصْبِحُ أَنْظَفَ، وَثَانِيًا لِأَنَّ النَّاسَ سَيَمْشُونَ أَكْثَرَ.⁩
Yāsmīn: I am in favour of closing down the center to cars. First, because the air will become cleaner; Second, because people will walk more.
⁧لُوكَا: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ التَّلَوُّثَ مُشْكِلَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ، إِلَّا أَنَّ الإِغْلَاقَ الكَامِلَ سَيَضُرُّ بِالمَحَلَّاتِ الصَّغِيرَةِ.⁩
Luca: It is true that pollution is a big problem, but total closure will damage small shops.
⁧يَاسْمِين: هٰذَا مَا يُقَالُ دَائِمًا، لٰكِنَّ التَّجَارِبَ تُثْبِتُ العَكْسَ. فِي مُدُنٍ كَثِيرَةٍ ارْتَفَعَتْ مَبِيعَاتُ المَحَلَّاتِ بَعْدَ إِغْلَاقِ الشَّوَارِعِ.⁩
Yāsmīn: That's what they always say, but experiences show the opposite. In many cities, sales of shops have increased after street closures.
⁧أَيُّ مُدُنٍ؟ وَهَلْ هِيَ مِثْلُ مِيلَانُو؟⁩ …« ⁧فِي مُدُنٍ كَثِيرَةٍ⁩ » ⁧لُوكَا:⁩
Luke: In many cities... which cities? And I'm like Milan?
⁧يَاسْمِين: حَسَنًا، نُقْطَةٌ لَكَ. يَجِبُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَ أَمْثِلَةً مُحَدَّدَةً.⁩
Yāsmīn: All right, I'll take you. I have to give specific examples.
⁧لُوكَا: وَأَنَا لَا أُنْكِرُ أَنَّ المَشْيَ مُفِيدٌ، غَيْرَ أَنَّ كِبَارَ السِّنِّ وَذَوِي الإِعَاقَةِ يَحْتَاجُونَ إِلَى حُلُولٍ.⁩
Luca: And I don't deny that walking is good, but the elderly and people with disabilities need solutions.
⁧يَاسْمِين: مُتَّفِقَةٌ. إِذَنْ لَيْسَ الحَلُّ فِي الإِغْلَاقِ الكَامِلِ، بَلْ فِي إِغْلَاقٍ تَدْرِيجِيٍّ مَعَ حَافِلَاتٍ صَغِيرَةٍ مَجَّانِيَّةٍ.⁩
Yāsmīn: All right. Then the solution is not total closure, but a gradual closure with small free buses.
So... we agree! This is not a discussion, it is a negotiation.

8. Pronunciation and Prosody

You can hear the concession. In reading aloud, the first part of a concession rises and remains suspended; the second ( ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ …, ⁧فَإِنَّ⁩ ...) descends forcefully: ṣaḥīḥun anna l-mašrūʿa mukliful ... illā anna fawāʾidahu akbar . Exercise on the examples of the section 4. ⁧إِلَّا أَنَّ⁩ pronunciation illā anna, with the double and long: don't confuse it with ⁧إِلَى أَنْ⁩ ( ilā An, ... until ...).
